title: Burdock root decoction for acne
subtitle: A long-course decoction of Arctium lappa root for acne and skin congestion
excerpt: Burdock root decoction is a 20-minute simmer of dried Arctium lappa root in water, taken twice daily as a long-course internal preparation for acne, skin congestion, and the chronic low-grade skin inflammation associated with hormonal or dietary acne. A bitter lymphatic and alterative herb traditionally used in European and Ayurvedic practice for skin conditions with an internal origin. Best taken for 8 to 12 weeks.
sourceNotes: Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), burdock entry, Botanical.com. Felter & Lloyd, King's American Dispensatory (1898), Arctium lappa entry. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Arctium lappa L., radix (2011, EMA/HMPC/247620/2009), open access.

glossaryTerms.definition: A traditional herbal category for herbs thought to gradually improve tissue nutrition, lymphatic drainage, and the elimination of metabolic waste, historically used for chronic skin conditions, glandular congestion, and 'sluggish' states. Burdock, cleavers, and red clover are classic alteratives.

content.text: Burdock root herbal brew is dried Arctium lappa root simmered in water for 20 minutes, a traditional

preparation for acne and chronic skin congestion. In European herbal practice, burdock root has long been the first herb reached for when skin inflammation comes from within, the persistent, cystic, or hormonal acne pattern that topical preparations alone do not resolve. The root's bitter compounds support liver and lymphatic clearance. its inulin content feeds gut bacteria involved in oestrogen metabolism. A 20-minute simmer is needed to extract from the woody root. Mildly earthy and bitter, pleasant enough to drink twice daily.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Place 5 g of dried burdock root in a small saucepan with 300 ml of cold water. Bring to a simmer.
Simmer gently for 20 minutes. The liquid will reduce slightly and darken to a warm brown-gold.
Strain into a mug and drink warm. Drink one cup in the morning and one in the afternoon.
Two cups daily for 8 to 12 weeks. slow-acting system-supporter herbs act slowly. results are rarely seen before 6 to 8 weeks of consistent use.
Dried burdock root stores 12 months in a sealed tin. Decoct fresh for each cup or prepare a day's supply (two cups) at once and refrigerate the second cup.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use if you have an Asteraceae allergy. See a doctor for severe acne or acne that is causing scars. Also see a doctor if acne comes with irregular periods, hair loss, or excess hair growth. These symptoms may need specialist review.
